raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` decorates `per_block_cast_to_fp8` with a module-level `torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend="inductor")`. Building that wrapper calls `_TorchCompileInductorWrapper.get_compiler_config()`, which imports `torch._inductor.compile_fx` and `torch._inductor.async_compile`, so every process that imports this module loads most of the Inductor stack. The API server and the engine core import it through `vllm.forward_context` → `dp_utils` → `ubatch_utils`, but the function is only called while processing weights. This PR compiles it on first call instead. Part of #59433.

## Claims

- `import vllm.v1.engine.core` no longer loads `torch._inductor.async_compile`. On CUDA, the `torch._inductor` module count after that import drops from 198 to 17. The `vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` import drops by 561 modules on CPU.
- `per_block_cast_to_fp8` returns bit-identical results to the old compiled function, keeps its signature and defaults, and keeps `__wrapped__` (used by `tests/quantization/test_online.py`).
- Scope: worker modules still import Inductor through other module-level `torch.compile` uses (e.g. `vllm/v1/sample/ops/logprobs.py`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py`), and workers compile anyway. With the default `UniProcExecutor`, the engine core loads the worker, so there the import is deferred rather than avoided. The clear win is the API server process, and the engine core when workers run in separate processes.

## Validation

```bash
python3 tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py
pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_requantized_moe_reload
```

```text
# main
  File "vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py", line 1072, in <module>
    @torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=current_platform.simple_compile_backend)
  ...
  File "torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py", line 27, in <module>
    import torch._inductor.async_compile
ModuleNotFoundError: import of torch._inductor.async_compile halted; None in sys.modules
exit 1

# this PR
exit 0
```

On 1x NVIDIA B300 with vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a` and this patch applied (the patched function is identical to this branch; other parts of `deep_gemm.py` differ in unrelated functions):
- After `import vllm.v1.engine.core`: `torch._inductor.async_compile` loaded `True` → `False`, `torch._inductor` modules 198 → 17.
- Numerics: the new function equals `torch.compile(_per_block_cast_to_fp8, dynamic=True, backend="inductor")` bit for bit (fp8 bytes and scales) for shapes (256, 512), (200, 300) and (7168, 2048), with `use_ue8m0` False and True.
- GPU tests, same results on main and with this PR:

| test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py` | 326 passed, 1 failed, 154 skipped | 326 passed, 1 failed, 154 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py` | 25 passed, 3 skipped | 25 passed, 3 skipped |
| `tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py` | 90 passed | 90 passed |
| `tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_requantized_moe_reload` | 18 passed | 18 passed |

The one failure (`test_w8a8_block_fp8_torch_scaled_mm_matmul`, `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`) happens on main too.

On CPU (macOS, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): after `import vllm.v1.engine.core`, modules 4797 → 4236 and `torch._inductor` modules 207 → 24; `vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server` 4916 → 4355. `tests/utils_/test_deep_gemm_utils.py` and `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py`: 11 passed on main and with this PR. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run --files` (including mypy) pass on the changed files.

## Details

- `_compiled_per_block_cast_to_fp8` is a `functools.cache` factory that returns the `torch.compile` wrapper, and the public `per_block_cast_to_fp8` calls it. A race on the first call can build two wrappers at worst; Dynamo caches by code object, so it still compiles once.
- `functools.wraps(..., assigned=())` only sets `__wrapped__`, so the public function keeps its own name and still pickles by reference.
- All in-tree callers (`quantization/online/fp8.py`, `quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py`) run in `process_weights_after_loading`, not under Dynamo tracing or CUDA graph capture.
- CI: `lazy_imports.py` currently runs only in the `(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser` job, which is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (#63609). #64414 restores it.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes `per_block_cast_to_fp8`. #57310 (`env_override.py`) handles a different `torch._inductor` edge. It and my structured-output PR also edit the end of `lazy_imports.py`, so whichever lands later needs a trivial rebase.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to draft the change, the test and this description. I reviewed the changes, the measurements and the test results before submitting.

files.patch:
@@ -13,6 +13,8 @@
 # `cv2` can easily mess up the environment.
 # `openai` belongs to the frontend layer; `vllm.config` is imported by
 # every process and must not pull it in.
+# `vllm.utils.deep_gemm` is imported by the API server and the engine core
+# (via `vllm.forward_context`) and must not `torch.compile` at import time.
 module_names = ["torch._inductor.async_compile", "cv2", "openai"]
 
 # set all modules in `module_names` to be None.
@@ -23,3 +25,4 @@
 
 import vllm  # noqa
 import vllm.config  # noqa
+import vllm.utils.deep_gemm  # noqa

@@ -1069,8 +1069,7 @@ def get_tma_aligned_size(x: int, element_size: int) -> int:
 
 
 # Taken from https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/dd6ed14acbc7445dcef224248a77ab4d22b5f240/deep_gemm/utils/math.py#L38
-@torch.compile(dynamic=True, backend=current_platform.simple_compile_backend)
-def per_block_cast_to_fp8(
+def _per_block_cast_to_fp8(
     x: torch.Tensor, block_size: list[int] = DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE, use_ue8m0: bool = False
 ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
     fp8_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
@@ -1092,6 +1091,26 @@ def per_block_cast_to_fp8(
     )
 
 
+@functools.cache
+def _compiled_per_block_cast_to_fp8() -> Callable[
+    ..., tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
+]:
+    # Compiled on first use: a module-level `torch.compile` imports
+    # torch._inductor in every process that imports this module.
+    return torch.compile(
+        _per_block_cast_to_fp8,
+        dynamic=True,
+        backend=current_platform.simple_compile_backend,
+    )
+
+
+@functools.wraps(_per_block_cast_to_fp8, assigned=())
+def per_block_cast_to_fp8(
+    x: torch.Tensor, block_size: list[int] = DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE, use_ue8m0: bool = False
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    return _compiled_per_block_cast_to_fp8()(x, block_size, use_ue8m0)
+
+
